'''Raghavan Varadarajan''' (born 27 November 1960) is an Indian biophysicist and a professor at the [[Indian Institute of Science]].<ref name="Executive Profile">{{cite web | url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=62440095&privcapId=248215062 | title=Executive Profile | publisher=Bloomberg | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref> He is known for his researches in the fields of protein structure and [[protein folding]]<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=98 | title=Brief Profile of the Awardee | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref> and his contributions in developing vaccines and drugs for treating a type of fatal [[influenza]] and [[HIV-1]].<ref name="Fighting the flu virus">{{cite web | url=http://m.deccanherald.com/articles.php?name=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.deccanherald.com%2Fcontent%2F80924%2Ffighting-flu-virus.html | title=Fighting the flu virus | newspaper=Deccan Herald | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016 | archive-date=20 October 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161020040357/http://m.deccanherald.com/articles.php?name=http://www.deccanherald.com/content/80924/fighting-flu-virus.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> He is a former J. C. Bose National Fellow of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] and an elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Indian National Science Academy]].<ref name="Indian fellow - Varadarajan">{{cite web | url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=P07-1450 | title=Indian fellow - Varadarajan | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=11 October 2016}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 2002, for his contributions to biological sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=201 | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Born on 27 November 1960,<ref name="Fellow profile - Varadarajan">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Varadarajan,_Prof._Raghavan | title=Fellow profile - Varadarajan | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=6 October 2016}}</ref> Raghavan Varadarajan completed his graduate and master's degrees from the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]] in 1982 and moved to the US for his doctoral studies at [[Stanford University]] under the guidance of Steven G. Boxer to secure a PhD.<ref name="Indian fellow - Varadarajan" /> His post-doctoral studies were at [[Yale University]] at the laboratory of [[Frederic M. Richards]] during 1988–92 and he returned to India to start his academic career at the [[Indian Institute of Science]] (IISc) in 1992. Holding the position of a professor of Molecular Biophysics Unit,<ref name="Professor Molecular Biophysics Unit">{{cite web | url=http://bio.iisc.ac.in/?q=faculty/raghavan-varadarajan | title=Professor Molecular Biophysics Unit | publisher=Indian Institute of Science | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref> he heads ''The Varadarajan Laboratory'' of IISc which has research interests in the design of [[HIV-1]] and [[influenza]] [[immunogen]]s.<ref name="Varadarajan Laboratory">{{cite web | url=http://mbu.iisc.ernet.in/~rvgrp/ | title=Varadarajan Laboratory | publisher=Indian Institute of Science | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref> He also serves as an honorary professor at [[Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research]]<ref name="Faculty members">{{cite web | url=http://www.jncasr.ac.in/cbumain.php/Faculty-members/1/1/ | title=Faculty members | publisher=Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref> and as the chairman of the scientific board of ''Theramyt Novobiologics'', a [[Bengaluru]]-based research platform (which he helped found), engaged in the development of [[biological drug]]s.<ref name="Founding team">{{cite web | url=http://theramyt.com/founding-team/ | title=Founding team | publisher=Theramyt Novobiologics | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016 | archive-date=20 October 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161020041103/http://theramyt.com/founding-team/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Legacy ==
Varadarajan's early researches were focused on the interaction of protein molecules and their sequential properties.<ref name="Lack of good students worries Bhatnagar awardees">{{cite web | url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/Lack-of-good-students-worries-Bhatnagar-awardees/articleshow/24995719.cms | title=Lack of good students worries Bhatnagar awardees | publisher=Times of India | date=12 October 2002 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref> At Steven G. Boxer's laboratory, he worked on human [[myoglobin]], a [[hemeprotein]], and studied its dielectric properties as well as the ''redox potential/spectral properties of bound chromophores''.<ref name="Cloning, Expression in Escherichia coli, and Reconstitution of Human Myoglobin">{{cite journal | jstor=26170| title=Cloning, Expression in Escherichia coli, and Reconstitution of Human Myoglobin | author=Raghavan Varadarajan, Alex Szabo and Steven G. Boxer | journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences | date=September 1985 | volume=82 | issue=17 | pages=5681–5684 | doi=10.1073/pnas.82.17.5681| pmc=390615 | pmid=3898068| bibcode=1985PNAS...82.5681V | doi-access=free }}</ref> Later, during his post-doctoral days at Yale, he researched on the ''structural and thermodynamic changes associated with cavity formation in proteins''.<ref name="Indian fellow - Varadarajan" /> Continuing his researches at IISc, he is known to have developed a new [[crystallographic]] and [[Nuclear magnetic resonance]] hydrogen exchange protocol for the characterization of disordered states of proteins,<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=5 October 2016 | pages=34 | archive-date=4 March 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref> and his studies helped in the estimation of the ''hydrophobic driving force in protein folding''. Collaborating with Merck Research Laboratories on behalf of [[Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research]], his team developed a number of [[immunogen]]s which have been demonstrated to have positive effect as HIV-1 vaccines<ref name="Fighting the flu virus" /> and he holds the patent for the invention.<ref name="HIV-1 Envelope Based Fragments">{{cite web | url=http://www.patentsencyclopedia.com/app/20110217338 | title=HIV-1 Envelope Based Fragments | publisher=Patents Encyclopedia | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref> Merck have tested the a few vaccines and some of the other proposals are being tested by [[International AIDS Vaccine Initiative]].<ref name="Summary of Achievements">{{cite web | url=http://www.serb.gov.in/pdfs/research/Prof_Raghavan_Varadarajan.pdf | title=Summary of Achievements | publisher=Science and Engineering Research Board, Government of India | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref>

Varadarajan has published his research findings by way of several articles{{Refn|group=note|Please see Selected bibliography section}} and his publications have been listed in a number of online article repositories.<ref name="Raghavan Varadarajan on ScienceOpen">{{cite web | url=https://www.scienceopen.com/user/24001469-aedb-4b36-abf0-4fdb3eb2ecc5/other-publications | title=Raghavan Varadarajan on ScienceOpen | publisher=ScienceOpen | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref><ref name="Citing TSpred Server">{{cite web | url=http://mspc.bii.a-star.edu.sg/TSpred/Reference.html | title=Citing TSpred Server | publisher=Bioinformatics Institute | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref><ref name="All Publications">{{cite web | url=https://web.stanford.edu/group/boxer/all_pubs.html | title=All Publications | publisher=Boxer Lab | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref> He served as an investigator of the ''DBT-IAVI Programme'' jointly organized by the Department of Biotechnology and [[International AIDS Vaccine Initiative]] for the development of HIV vaccines.<ref name="New Indian Medicinal Chemistry Programme towards Advancement of Novel Neutralizing Antibody Approach">{{cite web | url=http://www.iavi.org/press-releases/2007/213-india-s-department-of-biotechnology-and-iavi-forge-partnership | title=New Indian Medicinal Chemistry Programme towards Advancement of Novel Neutralizing Antibody Approach | publisher=International AIDS Vaccine Initiative | date=2 May 2007 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref> He has also mentored a number of scholars in their doctoral researches<ref name="Indian fellow - Varadarajan" /> and has conducted seminars on his researches.<ref name="Seminar by Prof. Raghavan Varadarajan">{{cite web | url=http://www.bbk.ac.uk/biology/about-us/events/seminar-by-prof.-raghavan-varadarajan-friday-3-july-2015 | title=Seminar by Prof. Raghavan Varadarajan | publisher=Department of Biological Sciences, University of London | date=2015 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref><ref name="Speakers">{{cite web | url=http://www.presiuniv.ac.in/web/molecuetosystemspk.php | title=Speakers | publisher=Presidency University | date=2016 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Varadarajan received the B. M. Birla Science Award of the [[Birla Science Museum|B. M. Birla Science Centre]] in 1998 for his contributions to the study of protein structure and foldings<ref name="Birla awards for young scientists ">{{cite web | url=http://www.thehindu.com/2001/12/19/stories/2001121901661300.htm | title=Birla awards for young scientists | date=19 December 2001 | work=[[The Hindu]] | access-date=19 October 2016}}{{dead link|date=September 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> and the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (CSIR) awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 2002.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees" /> In 2013, CSIR honored him again with the G. N. Ramachandran Gold Medal for Excellence in Biological Sciences and Technology.<ref name="G.N. Ramachandran Gold Medal for Excellence in Biological Sciences & Technology 2013">{{cite web | url=http://www.niscair.res.in/sciencecommunication/RnDNewsLetters/csirnews2k13/csirnews_oct13.pdf | title=G.N. Ramachandran Gold Medal for Excellence in Biological Sciences & Technology 2013 | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=October 2013 | access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref> He received a number of research fellowships which included the Swarnajayanthi Fellowship for Biological Sciences of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] and [[HIV/AIDS|AIDS]]-Innovation Grant Award of the [[National Institutes of Health]] ( both in 1999), Senior Research Fellowship of Wellcome Trust (2000) and the J. C. Bose National Fellowship of the Department of Science and Technology (2007–12).<ref name="Indian fellow - Varadarajan" /> He is also an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Fellow profile - Varadarajan" /> In 2024, Varadarajan became a laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]] by the ''[[Asian Scientist]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.asianscientist.com/as100/ |title=The Asian Scientist 100 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= |publisher= [[Asian Scientist]] |access-date= 13 March 2025 |quote= |language= }}</ref>
